# Three engine workflows stop on 2 December without an Actions policy

## Context

From 2 December 2026 GitHub blocks the `pull_request_target` event by default in every public repository, unless an applicable Actions event policy allows it ([changelog, 2026-11-02](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-02-pull_request_target-blocked-by-default-december-2/), [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target#default-policy-for-pull_request_target)). The rule runs in evaluate mode until then. **Its last rehearsal is a brownout today, 16 November, 16:00 to 18:00 UTC:** a blocked attempt becomes a failed run with an error annotation, and the workflow does not execute.

The engine is in scope: the organisation's audit log of 2026-11-15 holds 132 `workflows.actions_policy_violation` rows for `neomjs/neo`, all with `event_name: pull_request_target`, `is_evaluate_mode: true` and `allowed: true`.

## The Problem

Three workflows in this repository start on that event, and each is first contact with an outside contributor:

| Workflow | `pull_request_target` types | What stops |
|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` | `opened`, `reopened`, `edited`, `closed` | A pull request on an unclaimed curated issue no longer counts as its claim; no overlap or release notice (#21022) |
| `.github/workflows/merge-comment.yml` | `closed` | A merged outside pull request gets no comment with its standing, badge and next issues (#20893) |
| `.github/workflows/review-admission-mergeability.yml` | `opened`, `reopened`, `synchronize`, `ready_for_review` on `dev` | No admission status at a pull request event; a conflicted pull request gets no `pull_request` run at all, so nothing else reports it (#17692) |

No other repository of the organisation has a workflow on the trigger on its default branch (code search over `neomjs` on 2026-11-16: these three files, every other hit is a spec). Private repositories are outside the rule.

**Two more are on the way (added 2026-11-16T01:37Z).** The parity pull requests neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1778 and neomjs/neo-agent-institution#996 add `pull_request_target` (`opened`, `reopened`, `edited`, `closed`) to each repository's `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml`. Both repositories are public. From their merge on, each is under the same block.

On 9 November, 67 seconds into the first brownout, run [42650459962](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42650459962) still succeeded. One run decides nothing; today's window does.

## The Architectural Reality

The trigger stays. Each use is a recorded decision:
- #17692: an ordinary `pull_request` workflow does not run while a pull request conflicts, so mergeability needs `pull_request_target`.
- #20893 and #21022: the run needs the base repository's token for a fork's pull request and no run approval, or a first-time contributor's claim and comment wait for a maintainer.

All three keep GitHub's safe shape: the workflow file comes from the default branch, `claim-responder.yml` and `merge-comment.yml` sparse-check out two default-branch modules with `persist-credentials: false`, `review-admission-mergeability.yml` checks out nothing, and no step executes code from a pull request's head. That is the case the platform's own remedy names: "Explicitly allow `pull_request_target` in an applicable Actions event policy if your workflows depend on it. Use workflow file targeting to allow specific workflows."

## The Fix

One Actions policy on `neomjs/neo`, set by a repository administrator (Settings → Actions → Policies):
- enforcement **Active**;
- targeted at the three workflow paths above, not at all workflows;
- events allowed: `pull_request_target` **and every other event these three files declare**: `issue_comment`, `push`, `workflow_run`, `workflow_dispatch`.

An event rule is an allowlist. A policy left on all workflows, or one that names `pull_request_target` alone, blocks runs that work today.

Once the two parity pull requests are merged, the same policy in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` and in `neomjs/neo-agent-institution`: one workflow path, `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml`, events `pull_request_target` and `issue_comment`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 (human step, @tobiu as repository administrator):** the policy above exists on `neomjs/neo`.
- [ ] **AC-1b (human step, @tobiu):** after the sibling callers neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1801 and neomjs/neo-agent-institution#1008 are merged (they replaced the closed neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1778 and neomjs/neo-agent-institution#996), each of the two repositories has its policy for `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml`. Until then their claim responders keep running on `issue_comment` alone.
- [ ] **AC-2 (Mnemosyne, right after AC-1):** nothing else stopped. The next run of each of the three workflows ends as before, and a `pull_request`, a `push` and an `issue_comment` run still start: `gh run list --repo neomjs/neo --created ">=<policy time>" --json event,workflowName,conclusion`. Recorded here.
- [x] **AC-3, the proof that holds on 2 December:** *Met in its second form on 2026-11-16: no policy was in place, and 64 of 64 `pull_request_target` runs of the three files failed at startup inside the window ([final read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21069#issuecomment-6924749523)).* if the policy is in place before 16:00 UTC today, no `pull_request_target` run fails inside the brownout (`gh run list --repo neomjs/neo --event pull_request_target --created "2026-11-16T16:00:00Z..2026-11-16T18:00:00Z"`, read by Mnemosyne). If it lands later, the window's failures are recorded as the measured effect, and the proof is the repository's Policy insights page showing no would-block entry for the three workflows (human step, @tobiu).

## Out of Scope

- Changing any workflow's trigger or code.
- An organisation-level policy. Three repository policies keep a mistake inside one repository; an organisation policy with a wrong target reaches all of them. In every other public repository the default block is the safer state.
- A spec that pins the list of workflows on the trigger: a blocked run fails loudly, with an annotation that names the policy.

## Avoided Traps

- **Rebuilding the three on `workflow_run`.** A first-time contributor's `pull_request` runs wait for approval and a conflicted pull request has none, so the chained run would come late or never (#17692, #20893).
- **Setting the policy through the REST API from a seat.** The endpoints need repository administration; this seat's token gets a 404 on the read.
- **Waiting for 2 December to find out.** After today there is no rehearsal left.

### @neo-fable-mnemosyne - 2026-11-16T16:19:52Z

**Interim read during the last brownout, 2026-11-16T16:15:42Z** (the window runs 16:00 to 18:00 UTC). No repository policy is in place, so this is the measured effect of 2 December.

| Workflow | `pull_request_target` runs since 16:00Z | Other events |
|---|---|---|
| `claim-responder.yml` | 6 of 6 `startup_failure`, the first 43903008013 at 16:02:18Z | `issue_comment` runs complete as before |
| `merge-comment.yml` | 4 of 4 `startup_failure`, the first 43903005609 at 16:02:17Z | `workflow_dispatch` runs complete (below) |
| `review-admission-mergeability.yml` | 2 of 2 `startup_failure` (43904706698, 43905181991) | `push` runs succeed |

The last successful `pull_request_target` runs were 43902436577 at 15:59:17Z (claim responder) and 43902158420 at 15:57:45Z (review admission).

**What the window dropped so far.** One outside merge: #21128 at 16:08:09Z got no merge comment (run 43904120430). I replayed it through the workflow's own dispatch path: render-only run 43905680073, posting run 43906076650, [comment 6922101066](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21128#issuecomment-6922101066) at 16:19:04Z. The three other merges in the window were the team's (`#21124`, `#21149`, `#21150`) and get no comment by design. One pull request opened, the team's `#21153`. No outside opening and no unmerged close so far.

**For AC-1:** only the `pull_request_target` event is affected. `issue_comment`, `push` and `workflow_dispatch` runs of the same three files start normally inside the window.

**Until 18:00 UTC:** an outside pull request that merges gets its comment by `gh workflow run merge-comment.yml --repo neomjs/neo --ref dev -f pr=<n> -f post=true` (it refuses a second comment on the same pull request). An outside opening or unmerged close has no replay path in `claim-responder.yml`; I list those in the final read after the window.

### @neo-fable-mnemosyne - 2026-11-16T18:04:31Z

**Final read of the last brownout (2026-11-16, 16:00 to 18:00 UTC), taken at 18:03:14Z.** No repository policy was in place during the window.

| Workflow | `pull_request_target` runs in the window | Other events in the window | First `pull_request_target` run after it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claim-responder.yml` | 31 of 31 `startup_failure` | `issue_comment`: 38 completed | 43924697391 at 18:02:52Z, started |
| `merge-comment.yml` | 12 of 12 `startup_failure` | `workflow_dispatch`: 6 success | 43924697199 at 18:02:52Z, started |
| `review-admission-mergeability.yml` | 21 of 21 `startup_failure` | `push`: 10 success, 2 cancelled; `workflow_dispatch`: 1 success | 43924329615 at 18:00:47Z, success |

**What the window dropped, and what became of it.**

- **Merge comments.** 12 pull requests merged in the window, 4 of them from outside the team. Each of the four has its comment now, by the workflow's dispatch path: `#21128` (6922101066, 16:19:04Z), `#21014` (6924476456, 17:52:55Z), `#21134` (6924485261, 17:53:16Z), `#21034` (6924631866, 17:59:28Z). The first by me, the other three by Emmy. One caveat for any later replay: the first dispatch for `#21034` ended green and posted nothing, after a secondary rate limit of the search API; its retry posted. A green replay run is no receipt, the comment is.
- **Claim handling on openings.** 6 pull requests opened in the window, 2 from outside: `#21154` (closes `#21143`) and `#21158` (closes `#21157`). Neither target carries a curated label, so the responder would not have acted. Nothing was lost.
- **Unmerged closes.** None, so no release notice was due.
- **Comment claims** ran throughout.

**AC-3** is met in its second form: the 64 startup failures (31 + 12 + 21) are the measured effect of running without the policy. From 2 December that is the permanent state of the three files on pull-request events: no merge comment, no opening taken as a claim, no release notice, no review-admission run.

**AC-1** stays open and is the operator's: one repository policy for the three paths. AC-2, my collateral read, follows it.
